description: We are Space Sounds, a creative and passionate team participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 in Mumbai. We are building SOUND OF TIMES, an interactive jukebox that transforms real NASA Earth and space data into music, soundscapes and immersive visual experiences. We love combining technology, science, creativity and storytelling to make scientific discoveries fun and accessible. We welcome teammates interested in coding, data science, design, animation, audio and storytelling!
summary:
For this challenge, we developed Sound  of Time, a retro pixel art game where players uncover a vintage jukebox on an alien planet and play back memories of Earth.

Rather than just playing sound effects, the jukebox runs on real NASA Earth Science data. We wrote a synthesis engine that takes live satellite inputs forest canopy structure from GEDI, ocean currents and temperatures from ECCO, and atmospheric data from MERRA 2 and translates those numbers directly into musical notes, chords, and procedural soundscapes in real time.

Scientific data is usually visual and hard for non experts to digest. By turning raw planetary measurements into interactive audio wrapped in an engaging story, our project turns complicated numbers into an experience anyone can intuitively hear, understand, and connect with.
details:
1. What It Does & How It Works

Sound of Time is a playable 2D pixel art narrative game and interactive sonification platform built directly in the browser.

The story follows an astronaut, Ryan, living far from Earth on the planet Erid alongside his alien companion, Rocky. After discovering an antique jukebox buried in the alien terrain, they bring it back to their habitat to play archive cylinders sent from Earth.

Behind the retro pixel art aesthetic lies a real time procedural audio engine. Rather than playing pre recorded audio files, the jukebox translates real NASA Earth observation datasets into music on the fly:

  • Forest (NASA GEDI L4B & L3): Space station laser altimeter data (canopy height, foliage diversity, and biomass density) controls an Earth Lydian melodic scale, polyphonic arpeggios, and synthesized acoustic layers (rustling leaves, canopy wind gusts, and dawn bird choruses).
  • Ocean (NASA ECCO V4r4): Potential temperature, salinity, and horizontal current velocities drive oceanic Dorian synth chords, FM overtone brightness, and stereo wave surges.
  • Atmosphere (NASA MERRA-2 & AIRS): Aerosol optical depth and atmospheric pressure shape ambient wind filters, rain cadences, and harmonic tension.
  • Whole Earth Archive: Combines biosphere, hydrosphere, and atmosphere data into a unified polyphonic composition with a nostalgic piano theme.
  • AI Visual Scanner: Players can also drag and drop any NASA satellite image to scan its pixel luminance and color spectrum into live sound.

2. Benefits & Accessibility

  • Multi Sensory Science: Provides an auditory, intuitive way for visually impaired individuals, non scientists, and students to experience satellite data without needing to decipher complex graphs.
  • Zero Friction Access: Runs 100% client side in standard web browsers with zero installations, no backend server, and no large downloads. It works offline out of the box.
  • Scientific Transparency: Every record includes an in game science HUD and documentation panel displaying the exact NASA mission, DOI, variable ranges, and mathematical mapping formulas used.

3. Intended Impact

Climate and satellite data often feel cold, technical, and detached when viewed as static charts. Our goal was to make planetary science emotionally resonant and universally accessible. By pairing real environmental measurements with a story about memory, friendship, and homesickness, Sound of Time turns abstract numbers into living sound, inspiring curiosity and empathy for Earth's interconnected ecosystems.

4. Tools, Languages & Technology

  • Languages: Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5 Canvas 2D, and CSS3.
    • NASA GEDI L4B (DOI: 10.5067/GEDI/GEDI04_B.002)
    • NASA ECCO V4r4 (DOI: 10.5067/ECG5D-OTS44)
    • NASA MERRA-2 (DOI: 10.5067/95140KBM4KUS)
    • NASA SVS visual presets (SVS 3912, SVS 5313, SVS 4252)
  • Development & Version Control: Visual Studio Code, Git, GitHub, and browser developer tools.

5. Creative Choices & Design Decisions

Instead of creating a conventional, sterile scientific dashboard, we wrapped the data in an engaging narrative game. The player isn’t just analyzing numbers they are exploring an alien world and sharing the memories of their home planet with an alien friend.

Aesthetically, we blended 1950s vacuum tube jukebox hardware with futuristic space exploration. Musically, we avoided harsh data sonification "noise" by anchoring the numbers to harmonic musical scales (Lydian and Dorian) alongside procedural nature sounds modeled after U.S. National Park Service acoustic ecology recordings. The result sounds like actual music that breathes with real planetary data.

6. Factors Our Team Considered

  • Balancing Accuracy with Musicality: Direct 1:1 frequency mapping often sounds chaotic. We carefully calibrated normalization functions so that real data trends (such as temperature rises or canopy height changes) produce musically pleasing, distinct shifts.
  • Performance & Reliability: We avoided external audio assets that could fail to load or buffer over poor internet connections. Synthesizing 100% of the audio procedurally in code guarantees instant loading and responsive interaction on any device.
  • Layered Engagement: We designed the project with two depths: casual players can simply enjoy the 6 8 minute story, while curious learners and judges can dive into the live HUD to inspect the exact mathematical curves and scientific attribution.
